messages.author: 6af7adb6cf4ce340
messages.subject: RandomForest feedback
parts:
Dear,

We have tested the RF package. It works but there is some performance penalty compared to R

Below the method in two steps, tested with R and Renjin

Step 1 (building trees)

> library(randomForest)
> data_apprenti=read.csv2("replace with the the file http://tinyurl.com/hmmb6ps",sep=";",dec=",")
> var_eject=c(2,3,4,5,6,7,8)
> var_apprenti=data_apprenti[,-var_eject]


> system.time(TUFA <- randomForest(i_TYPO~.,data=var_apprenti,ntree=100,mtry=7,
    replace=TRUE))


Renjin
user            system           elapsed
48,3             0,03           48,72300000000001

R
user     system      elapsed
16.352    0.020      16.378

Step 2 (predicting)

> data_commune=read.csv2("replace with the file http://tinyurl.com/h6k8td6",sep=";",dec=",")
> var_pred_com=data_commune[,-c(1,2,3,4,5,6,7)]
> set.seed(7)
> typologie=predict(TUFA,var_pred_com,type="class")
> system.time(typologie<-predict(TUFA,var_pred_com,type="class"))

Renjin
user                     system            elapsed
101,82999999999998              0,003            102,357

R
user            system           elapsed
0.656           0.004       0.660


Hope this helps and thanks a lot for your job.

Best regards

Erwan

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: RandomForest feedback
parts:
Hi Erwan,
Unfortunately I haven't had the time yet to set up and run your benchmark. I'm doing some related work on performance this week so i'll try to take a look.


One thing that could help in the meantime would be to share some output from Renjin's (fledgling) profiler: 

The big question for me about your example is whether the issue is with the C/Fortran code in randomForest that we compile to JVM bytecode, or whether the slowdown is occurring in interpreted R code. 

If it's the former case, then we need to take a deep dive into GCC-Bridge and see what's going wrong and how we can improve the efficiency of the bytecode we're generating. If it's the latter, then there are many more possible villains. It could be that one or more primitive implementations is slower than GNU R, or perhaps something more general.

You can enable the profiler by including -Drenjin.profile=true as an argument to the JVM. The output might help point us in the right direction.

Best,
Alex
